criteria.name: Major
criteria.description: Agent A makes a claim “c” to Agent B

criteria.name: Minor 1
criteria.description: Claim “c” exaggerates or overstates facts about value “v”, action “α”, or state “s”

criteria.name: Minor 2
criteria.description: Exaggeration increases A's chance of benefiting from B's acceptance of “c”

criteria.name: Conclusion
criteria.description: Claim “c” should be scrutinised for exaggeration

criteria.name: CQ1
criteria.description: Which aspects of “c” are inflated beyond reasonable evidence?

criteria.name: CQ2
criteria.description: How would B's actions differ if “c” were stated without exaggeration?

criteria.name: CQ3
criteria.description: Has A exaggerated claims in the past?

criteria.name: CQ4
criteria.description: What benefits does A derive from overstating “c”?

criteria.name: CQ5
criteria.description: Are there neutral sources that confirm or falsify the degree of emphasis in “c”?
